subtitle: The most fundamental spatial effect. Reverb simulates acoustic spaces, from intimate rooms to vast cathedrals, adding depth and dimension to your sound.

introduction.title: What is Reverb?
introduction.text: Reverb is the persistence of sound in a space after the original sound stops. In nature, reverb occurs when sound waves reflect off surfaces in an environment. Reverb effects simulate these reflections, creating the impression of playing in different spaces.

columns.title: Components of Reverb
columns.text: Early reflections: First echoes off surfaces. Late reflections: Dense reverb tail. Decay time: How long reverb lasts. Pre-delay: Gap before reverb starts. Diffusion: Echo density and smoothness.

columns.title: Musical Functions
columns.text: Creates sense of space and depth. Smooths harsh transients. Adds sustain to notes. Enhances emotional impact. Glues instruments together. Provides ambient texture.

cards.title: Spring Reverb
cards.description: Mechanical reverb using metal springs. Classic surf and rockabilly sound with distinctive "boing" character.

fields.label: Found in
fields.value: Fender amps, outboard spring tanks, pedals

cards.title: Plate Reverb
cards.description: Large metal plates create smooth, dense reverb. Studio standard from the 1960s-80s with distinctive bright character.

cards.title: Hall Reverb
cards.description: Simulates large acoustic spaces like concert halls. Long decay times and natural-sounding reflections.

cards.title: Room Reverb
cards.description: Intimate acoustic spaces with shorter decay times. Natural-sounding reverb that doesn't overwhelm the dry signal.

fields.label: Best for
fields.value: Adding space without clouding the mix

cards.title: Chamber Reverb
cards.description: Echo chambers used in classic recordings. Warm, musical reverb with distinctive character.

cards.title: Algorithmic Reverb
cards.description: Digital reverbs that create artificial spaces through mathematical algorithms. Highly controllable and versatile.

cards.title: Lexicon 480L
cards.description: The gold standard of digital reverb. Used on countless hit records from the 1980s onward. Incredibly musical algorithms.

fields.label: Signature Sound
fields.value: Lush, musical digital reverbs with excellent diffusion and natural decay

cards.title: EMT 140 Plate Reverb
cards.description: The original and most famous plate reverb. Massive 4x8 foot metal plates created the smooth, dense reverb heard on classic recordings.

fields.label: Signature Sound
fields.value: Smooth, dense reverb with bright character and musical decay

cards.title: Fender Spring Reverb
cards.description: Built into classic Fender amplifiers. The iconic "drip" sound of surf music and rockabilly. Mechanical and characterful.

fields.label: Signature Sound
fields.value: Bright, splashy reverb with distinctive spring crash when amp is moved

items: Dick Dale - King of surf guitar

cards.title: Strymon BigSky
cards.description: Modern digital reverb pedal with studio-quality algorithms. Combines classic reverb types with modern innovations.

fields.label: Signature Sound
fields.value: High-quality digital reverbs with extensive tweakability and pristine sound

cards.title: Technical Tips
items: Place reverb last in signal chain

sections.title: Reverb Settings Guide
sections.warningText: The key to great reverb is restraint. Start with less than you think you need, then gradually add more. Reverb should enhance your sound, not dominate it.
